text:
Maya (Docs): heads up — opening a migration guide PR for dedicated capacity autoscale cooldown defaults (60s -> 300s). need quick eng review + a small SDK snippet + terraform example. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4822 preview: https://deploy-preview.example.com. target merge by EOD Fri. any blockers?

Alec (Eng Runtime): thanks. i'll review. does this change the burstPolicy semantics? we should call out preemption/race with reserved pools and any tenant isolation edgecases. also suggest a canary note.

Jules (DevEx): i can draft the python SDK snippet + terraform. which config path is this living under — autoscale.policy or capacity config?

Maya (Docs): it's under autoscale.policy -> cooldown_seconds. want examples showing implicit default vs explicit override. terraform module is redwood/dedicated_capacity (we have an existing example but needs updated fields). include tenant label sample and a canary recommendation.

Sam (Product): add SLA wording: "expected stabilization within 5 minutes for scale ops under normal load" and note fallback to reserved pool. include rollback steps (how to pin previous autoscale policy and force scale).

doc-bot: PR opened by @Maya — https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4822 :white_check_mark: CI: preview build succeeded.

Alec (Eng Runtime): small technical note — for low-latency chat workloads the longer cooldown can hurt cold-starts; recommend the docs include a guidance table: use 60s for chat with short sessions, 300s for bursty batch inference. i'll add a short paragraph and an inline example showing target metrics (p95 latency, queue depth).

Jules (DevEx): draft snippets below — feel free to paste into the PR (keeping minimal):
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient()
client.update_autoscale_policy(
    tenant="team-foo",
    policy={"min_replicas": 1, "max_replicas": 10, "cooldown_seconds": 300}
)
```
```hcl
module "dedicated" {
  source = "github.com/redwood/modules/dedicated"
  tenant = "team-foo"
  autoscale = {
    min = 1
    max = 10
    cooldown_seconds = 300
  }
}
```

Maya (Docs): awesome, thx. can you also add a one-line canary strategy: "start with 5% traffic for 30m, verify scaling and errors, then ramp"?

Jules (DevEx): added that line and a tiny checklist (observability: p95, error-rate, scaling-events). pushed a commit to the PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4822/files#diff-abc123

Alec (Eng Runtime): left an inline comment re: reserved_pool fallback wording — prefer "automatic fallback to reserved pool when target replicas cannot be provisioned within stabilization window". also small nit: rename section to "Stabilization windows".

Maya (Docs): will update wording and merge the checklist. who can do final lgtm? @Sam?

Sam (Product): i'll review this evening and merge if green. also will add the SLA blurb and a short product note for release notes. :thumbsup:

Maya (Docs): thanks all — i'll queue a follow-up to update handbook links and add a short migration note for customers with custom TF modules.

Alec (Eng Runtime): one follow-up — let's add a tiny troubleshooting snippet for tenants that see oscillation after increasing cooldown (suggest reducing cooldown or adjusting target metrics).

Jules (DevEx): ok will add a troubleshooting bullet.

Maya (Docs): perfect. closing on the PR later today unless any other issues crop up.
